question: Over the past few months, farmers in Réunion have expressed their concerns over the Commission’s classification of the Victoria pineapple as a ‘non-perennial variety’. This decision is undermining the island’s agricultural economy and contributing to a growing scarcity of the crop. The Victoria pineapple, Réunion’s agricultural jewel, now finds itself under threat.

It had been flourishing: the number of tonnes exported doubled between 2008 and 2018. Now, ARIFEL (the fruit and vegetable association in Réunion) has calculated that production fell by 1 500 tonnes between 2019 and 2022. Part of the reason is, of course, inflation in the price of agricultural plastic and fertilisers, leading to an overall increase in production costs of around EUR 20 000 per hectare in 2023.

However, pineapple production is now also being penalised by the EU ending its aid for new plantations. This support had been encouraging farmers to diversify into pineapple cultivation. In my view, the Commission should reconsider its classification of the Victoria pineapple. What action will the Commission take to remedy this situation and ensure the economic viability of pineapple production in Réunion?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2024) The 2014-2022 Réunion Rural Development Programme (RDP) supports cultivation of Victoria pineapples. Nevertheless, as the Honourable Member mentions, the production of Victoria pineapples fell between 2019 and 2022.

France’s Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan (CSP) 2023-2027 does not offer the possibility of supporting the financing of investments in new plantations in the pineapple sector. The choice of investments supported both through the RDP and the CSP lies with the Member State authorities and is based on an analysis of the national needs and the definition of a national strategy.
Investments in new pineapple plantations are also supported within the framework of the recovery plan for the years 2023-2024.

As regards POSEI1, aid for marketing outside the region of production, amounting to EUR 3 million per year for Réunion, also finances the marketing of pineapple production (irrespective of variety) under marketing contracts concluded by individual producers, an approved collective structure or a processor, on the one hand, and a purchaser outside the production region, on the other.

The Victoria variety is also monitored through the reference networks funded under POSEI. Whether or not to support Victoria pineapple production and the choice of instrument is a decision of the national and departmental authorities.
1 Programme of options specifically relating to remoteness and insularity.
